output.title: When spot checks stop working
output.body:
If you run a small business, spot checks work until they don’t. The warning sign is not that you are checking too little on purpose. It is that the same errors keep turning up, or new ones slip through between checks. Then the real question is not “should I inspect more?” but “which part of this workflow can be checked automatically, and which part must stay human?”

A good candidate is a repeatable document or data review with clear rules. Think invoice amounts against an expected limit, customer replies against a simple FAQ list, or recurring form fields that should match a known pattern. That is not about replacing judgment. It is about making the routine flagging consistent so you only review exceptions.

The boundary stays firm: money movement and other high-risk decisions still need human approval. Automation can sort, flag, and route. It should not approve on its own.

The practical next step is simple: name the one check that fails most often. That gives you a clear starting point for deciding whether the workflow needs a manual fix, a tighter rule, or an automated checkpoint.
